sessions.title: Recognize the two taught aspect pairs

steps.title: Aspect and time
steps.body: Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens. Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint. Perfective presents an event with its boundary or result. Imperfective does not by itself mean unfinished. говори́ть is imperfective; сказа́ть is perfective. These infinitives do not specify tense on their own.

steps.title: The saying and telling pair
steps.body: Many Russian verbs are learned in an aspect pair, but not every verb has two words, and a pair is not automatic. говорить and сказать are context-dependent counterparts, not a universal pair for the English verb speak. For the saying/telling pair shown here, the perfective counterpart of говори́ть is сказа́ть; the imperfective counterpart of сказа́ть is говори́ть. These checks ask you to recognize this vocabulary pair, not choose aspect in a sentence.

steps.title: A worked doing and making pair
steps.body: де́лать is imperfective; сде́лать is perfective. Both concern doing or making. The perfective focuses on accomplishing the action; the imperfective can describe the activity or its occurrence without that focus. Given де́лать and a request for its perfective counterpart, choose сде́лать. говори́ть concerns speaking or saying and belongs to the other pair. Learn the shown pair rather than assuming every prefix changes only aspect.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the counterpart from the saying/telling pair. Then compare its aspect and meaning with the other option.

steps.title: Review the two aspect pairs
steps.body:
Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens. Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint. Perfective presents an event with its boundary or result. Imperfective does not by itself mean unfinished. говори́ть is imperfective; сказа́ть is perfective. These infinitives do not specify tense on their own.

Many Russian verbs are learned in an aspect pair, but not every verb has two words, and a pair is not automatic. говорить and сказать are context-dependent counterparts, not a universal pair for the English verb speak. For the saying/telling pair shown here, the perfective counterpart of говори́ть is сказа́ть; the imperfective counterpart of сказа́ть is говори́ть. These checks ask you to recognize this vocabulary pair, not choose aspect in a sentence.

де́лать is imperfective; сде́лать is perfective. Both concern doing or making. The perfective focuses on accomplishing the action; the imperfective can describe the activity or its occurrence without that focus. Given де́лать and a request for its perfective counterpart, choose сде́лать. говори́ть concerns speaking or saying and belongs to the other pair. Learn the shown pair rather than assuming every prefix changes only aspect.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the first-person plural future?
items.feedback: Мы бу́дем говори́ть is the first-person plural future: the subject means we, and the future auxiliary agrees with that plural subject. Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular, meaning I. Both use a future auxiliary plus the same imperfective infinitive; choose the plural line requested here.
distractorRationales: Я бу́ду говори́ть has a first-person singular subject and auxiliary, rather than the requested first-person plural future.

distractorDifference: Я бу́ду говори́ть has a first-person singular subject and auxiliary, rather than the requested first-person plural future.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Мы бу́дем говори́ть is the first-person plural future: the subject means we, and the future auxiliary agrees with that plural subject. Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular, meaning I. Both use a future auxiliary plus the same imperfective infinitive; choose the plural line requested here.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the first-person singular future?
items.feedback: Я бу́ду говори́ть is the first-person singular future: the subject means I, and the future auxiliary agrees with one speaker. Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural, meaning we. The imperfective infinitive stays the same while the subject and auxiliary change.
distractorRationales: Мы бу́дем говори́ть has a first-person plural subject and auxiliary, rather than the requested first-person singular future.

distractorDifference: Мы бу́дем говори́ть has a first-person plural subject and auxiliary, rather than the requested first-person singular future.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: Я бу́ду говори́ть is the first-person singular future: the subject means I, and the future auxiliary agrees with one speaker. Мы бу́дем говори́ть is first-person plural, meaning we. The imperfective infinitive stays the same while the subject and auxiliary change.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the second-person plural future?
items.feedback: Вы бу́дете говори́ть is the second-person plural future row: the auxiliary agrees with you in that row. This form can also address one person politely. Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular and changes the person as well as the table number. The same imperfective infinitive follows each auxiliary.
distractorRationales: Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular future, not the requested second-person plural future row.

distractorDifference: Я бу́ду говори́ть is first-person singular future, not the requested second-person plural future row.

items.prompt: Which admitted line is the accepted spelling rather than the rejected example?
items.feedback: хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling in the source example. The adjective stem ends in the consonant transliterated sh; its unstressed neuter ending uses e rather than o under the five-letter spelling rule. хорошое письмо is the rejected counterexample and should not be used as correct Russian.
distractorRationales: хорошое письмо is the rejected spelling: it uses o where this unstressed adjective ending requires e.

distractorDifference: хорошое письмо is the rejected spelling: it uses o where this unstressed adjective ending requires e.
assessment.whyAnswerDemonstratesObjective: хорошее письмо is the accepted spelling in the source example. The adjective stem ends in the consonant transliterated sh; its unstressed neuter ending uses e rather than o under the five-letter spelling rule. хорошое письмо is the rejected counterexample and should not be used as correct Russian.
